description: Novacent is a multidisciplinary team focused on innovation and space exploration. For Challenge #3, we are developing an interactive map of Mars that integrates navigation, safety, and mobility features to help astronauts move safely across the Martian surface.
summary: How can a Mars crew compare two routes to a science stop? MARSWEAR is a web prototype developed by Team Novacent for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge. Using orbital imagery and elevation data from NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, the prototype compares a direct route and a detour to a boxwork formation on Mount Sharp in Gale crater. A simulated walk shows how a visor cue guides the crew at the fork and how a glove-friendly forearm display helps record observations at the science stop.
details:
Mission Overview

The simulated crew sets out to photograph a boxwork ridge and the adjacent hollow in Gale crater. The route planner combines a HiRISE orthoimage, a slope layer, and elevation profiles. A Mars Odyssey thermal infrared mosaic shows the site’s location within the crater.

Route Comparison

Route A covers 275.9 m round trip. Its steepest 5 m segment has a slope of 26°.

Route B covers 299.2 m round trip. Its steepest 5 m segment has a slope of 9°.

The prototype recommends Route B based on the team’s slope criteria. Side-by-side elevation profiles show where the extra 23.3 m of walking lets the crew avoid the steepest part of Route A.

Crew Workflow

Before departure, the crew compares both routes in the planner. At the fork, the visor gives a single direction cue. At the science stop, the forearm display shows a two-photo checklist. The module straps onto the suit’s outer cover, and its large confirmation button is positioned for use with the opposite hand while wearing gloves.

Tech Stack

QGIS for route mapping and terrain analysis using HiRISE data.

Figma for prototyping the route planner, visor, and forearm display.

HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the website and interactive route planner.
